newsitem.title: USA: McDougal says Clintons are lying on Whitewater.
newsitem.headline: McDougal says Clintons are lying on Whitewater.

text.p: James McDougal, sentenced to three years in prison on Whitewater-related charges, on Monday said U.S. President Bill Clinton and Hillary Rodham Clinton were lying about their role in the affair.

A White House spokeswoman declined to comment on McDougal's remarks, but Clinton on Friday said he was "not worried at all" at the possibility that McDougal could provide damaging evidence against him.

McDougal, appearing on CNN's "Larry King Live", reversed his earlier statements and said Clinton, then governor of Arkansas, did pressure a banker to extend a $300,000 loan to McDougal's ex-wife, Susan McDougal.

But he said Clinton did nothing illegal in the meeting with him and banker David Hale. "It was just embarrassing," McDougal said, although he described all three men as "con men" who "can say more with a wink and a nod."
Clinton under oath has denied pressuring Hale and said he did not recall any conversation about the loan.

McDougal was sentenced last week after agreeing to cooperate with Whitewater independent counsel Kenneth Starr. He had faced up to 81 years in prison for his conviction last May on 18 counts of fraud and conspiracy.
Asked why he lied in earlier statements, McDougal said, "I was protecting my president and my friend and myself." He said he and Clinton had known each other for nearly 30 years.

McDougal said in the hour-long interview that he began cooperating with Starr to "save my own skin" but became more helpful because he felt the president misled Susan McDougal into thinking she would be pardoned. She was sentenced to two years in prison for her part in winning the fraudulent loan.
Susan McDougal is serving a contempt of court sentence for refusing to testify before a grand jury.

McDougal said it was "entirely possible" Clinton and his then-wife were involved in an affair because Clinton's unexpected appearance at his meeting with Hale was "inexplicable" and no one besides his wife knew about it.

McDougal said he was "mystified" that his ex-wife went to jail rather than answer the grand jury's question, adding "I think there could be a personal and financial relationship" between the president and Susan McDougal.
McDougal also accused the first lady of lying about how she initially got involved in representing McDougal, saying, "I think she's been much less than truthful."

Hillary Clinton has insisted publicly that she got the work through a business associate at the Rose law firm in Arkansas, but McDougal said he discussed hiring Mrs. Clinton with the governor several hours before he met with her.
"I know she's lying," McDougal said, adding he hired Mrs. Clinton on a $2,000-a-month retainer to handle legal work, after the governor told him the firm faced a lot of expenses.
